message.content: Rowan describes Cersei's transformation as remarkable and complex, noting that she starts off as a "love-struck girl" but evolves into a "power-hungry queen." He emphasizes how Cersei's character is molded by the harsh realities of Westeros, specifically mentioning her loss of children, which pushes her to become ruthlessly ambitious. Rowan highlights the evolution of her relationship with power, observing how she initially appears vulnerable but quickly becomes ruthless, especially after losing her children. He notes that Cersei's journey showcases her ability to achieve her goals but also underscores the high cost she pays, suggesting that her pursuit of power comes at a personal cost. Rowan expresses his view that Cersei's arc in the series is wrapped up dramatically in the finale, yet he feels that it was somewhat rushed, wishing for more time to reflect on her choices.
